key_insight: By routing stabilizer ancillas along bespoke paths, the paper shows that surface-code quantum processors can remain fault tolerant even when about 10% of the physical lattice is damaged, with only a moderate drop in effective code distance.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical design path for semiconductor spin-qubit processors where fabrication defects or missing qubits are expected, suggesting oversized arrays can compensate for significant device damage.
method: Adapt the CAbLECAR stabilizer-execution scheme so each ancilla follows a pre-programmed route through the damaged lattice.
Use route-solving software to find commutation-preserving paths while avoiding hook-error propagation.
Convert the routed circuits into Stim detector error models and estimate logical error rates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that for reasonable physical error rates, 10% damage yields a reduced equivalent distance of about 0.48× the pristine lattice in the large-array limit, improving to about 0.60× for the smallest array studied.
watch_item: The approach depends on offline route planning under fixed damage patterns, so runtime defects or more complex hardware constraints could require additional adaptation.
paper_title: A route to damage tolerance exceeding $10\%$ in shuttling-equipped quantum processors
